messages.content: I’m ready to settle the Philadelphia flights. Compare the real round-trip totals and the terms, especially the Thursday timing. I don’t want to save a little money and then spend the whole final session watching the clock.

I rechecked the Monday, November 3 and Thursday, November 6 combinations from DFW. The practical comparison is between a $451 itinerary and a $497 all-nonstop itinerary. Before I book, I’ll walk through what changes between them, including baggage and the airport margins.
Start with Monday. Is the 6:20 flight still the best arrival for the Tuesday briefing?

Yes. The 6:20 p.m. nonstop reaches Philadelphia at 10:29 p.m. It is $219 in standard economy, includes a carry-on, and permits changes without a change fee, although any fare difference applies. The ticket is nonrefundable. The other nonstop leaves at 7:45 p.m. and arrives at 11:54 p.m.; its flexible fare is $254 and refundable to the original payment method. Either works for Tuesday morning, but the earlier arrival gives you a more reasonable hotel check-in.
Keep the 6:20. I can use a car from the airport. Now explain why the Thursday total changed from the $451 version we had.

The $451 version pairs that outbound with the 7:15 p.m. return through Atlanta. The schedule review surfaced a 7:05 p.m. nonstop arriving DFW at 9:39 p.m. That nonstop raises the round-trip airfare to $497. There is also a 5:05 p.m. nonstop that keeps the total at $414, but it would require leaving the convention area around 3:00 p.m. at the latest.
And the closing session ends at 3:00. I’d still have to go back for my suitcase, correct?

Correct. The hotel is about a seven-minute walk from the convention center. Even with the suitcase ready at the desk, the 5:05 flight would leave little recovery time for a delayed session, the walk, bag retrieval, or a missed train. The 7:05 nonstop supports leaving the venue after the session, collecting the bag, and reaching PHL with a comfortable margin.
What are the ticket rules on those two Thursday choices? I may need to check one suitcase both ways.

The 5:05 fare is basic economy: nonrefundable and not changeable after the 24-hour cancellation window. The 7:05 fare is standard economy: nonrefundable, but it can be changed with no change fee plus any fare difference. Both include a carry-on. One checked suitcase is $40 each direction if paid before check-in, so the complete air cost would be $577 with a checked bag round trip on the 7:05 option, or $494 on the 5:05 option.
Does the Atlanta itinerary have any advantage besides costing $46 less than the nonstop?

Not for this schedule. It leaves at 7:15 p.m., connects for 52 minutes in Atlanta, and arrives DFW at 11:31 p.m. Its standard-economy terms match the later nonstop, and the bag fees are the same. The $46 savings comes with a connection and an arrival nearly two hours later.
Then book the Monday 6:20 nonstop and Thursday 7:05 nonstop for $497. Use the traveler and payment information on file. Don’t add the checked bag yet.

Understood. I’m booking one round trip: DFW to PHL Monday, November 3 at 6:20 p.m., arriving 10:29 p.m.; PHL to DFW Thursday, November 6 at 7:05 p.m., arriving 9:39 p.m. The charge is $497. No checked baggage or other add-on is included.

The flights are ticketed under confirmation PHL6N8. The card on file was charged $497. The ticket is nonrefundable; changes are allowed without a change fee, with any fare difference due. You have a carry-on included, and no checked bag has been purchased. This fixes the Monday arrival and gives you enough time Thursday to attend the full closing session, retrieve the suitcase from the hotel, and head to the airport without relying on the earlier departure. The next planning step is to finalize the three-night hotel and confirm its Thursday luggage-storage arrangement.
